how: One real session of each tool in tmux, started with a per-session settings file (Claude Code) or -c notify=[...] (Codex). Text went in with tmux paste-buffer -p, then Enter.
facts: Claude Code: tmux paste-buffer -p followed by send-keys Enter submits a prompt. UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks fired about 3 seconds later.
Claude Code: the Stop hook input carries last_assistant_message, so the reply does not need the transcript. It also carries background_tasks.
Claude Code: hooks from --settings run next to the owner's own global hooks. They do not replace them.
Claude Code: the status line input carries context_window.used_percentage and rate_limits.five_hour / seven_day, each with used_percentage and resets_at in epoch seconds.
Claude Code: a new folder shows a trust question whose default answer is 'No, exit'. Enter there ends the session. The engine must never press Enter on that screen.
Claude Code: a folder inside a trusted folder shows no trust question.
Claude Code: --resume <session id> works; SessionStart then has source 'resume' and the same session_id.
Claude Code: a turn can end while a background shell still runs (Stop fires, background_tasks is not empty).
Claude Code: env CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT were unset for the child, because the capture ran from inside another Claude Code session.
Codex: -c 'notify=["<script>"]' runs the script at the end of each turn with one JSON argument: type agent-turn-complete, thread-id, turn-id, cwd, input-messages, last-assistant-message.

Codex: the rollout file has session_meta (id, cwd), event_msg task_started (turn_id, model_context_window), event_msg token_count (info.total_token_usage, rate_limits.primary.used_percent, window_minutes, resets_at) and event_msg task_complete (last_agent_message).
Codex: the first screen can be an update question whose default answer runs an installer. Escape skips it. The engine must never press Enter on that screen.
Codex: the rollout file path is ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<time>-<session id>.jsonl.
Not captured: what Claude Code or Codex emit when Escape interrupts a turn. Both test turns ended before the Escape arrived.

Claude Code: the status line input does not always carry rate_limits (see statusline-no-limits.json). Keep the newest value seen. statusline.json holds the values seen on 2026-11-11: five_hour 100, seven_day 73.
Codex: started with `-s workspace-write -a never`, a command inside the session reached a listener on 127.0.0.1 (curl gave 200). So a sandboxed Codex agent can call the engine.
Codex: in that sandbox, a write outside the workspace failed with 'Operation not permitted' (touch in the home folder, exit 1). No file was made.

Codex: `codex features list` shows `hooks` as stable and on. Hooks need persisted trust (there is a flag --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust). Starship does not use Codex hooks; it uses `notify` and the sandbox.

REAL RUN 2026-11-11, engine + real Claude Code (Haiku) as the admin agent of a chat with no repo: a message sent through POST /api/chats/:id/messages got the reply 'hello' in the chat in about 6 seconds.

Claude Code: the owner's own global hooks and plugins run inside every agent that Starship starts. A global Stop hook that blocks makes the agent go on working after its first Stop event: Claude Code then fires Stop a second time with stop_hook_active true. So one turn can give several Stop events with the same prompt_id.

Claude Code: --setting-sources project,local keeps user-level settings, hooks and plugins out of a session, and the --settings file still applies. But the owner's global CLAUDE.md rules are then NOT loaded either. Seen in a real session.

Claude Code: a dialog can open after a turn (seen: 'Teach auto mode about your environment?' with 'Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel', default 'Yes'). Escape closes it. A paste plus Enter while it is open would confirm it. See fixtures/claude/screens/dialog.txt.

Claude Code: a git worktree asks its own trust question even when it lies inside a trusted folder (seen for <home>/worktrees/<repo>/<slug>). Only a folder that is not a git root takes the trust of its parent.

Codex: a folder in a git project that Codex has not seen asks 'Trust this folder?' with '1. Trust and continue / 2. Quit' and 'enter continue · esc quit'. Trust applies to the repository root, so one answer covers every worktree of that repo. Escape QUITS Codex on this screen. See fixtures/codex/screens/trust.txt.

REAL RUN 2026-11-11, a build on a scratch repo: the Codex worker stopped at Codex's trust question (the engine took it for a screen to skip), and the Claude admin agent waited at Claude Code's trust question. The build did not move. Both must show as 'needs you: trust', and work must go on after the owner answers.

REAL RUN 2 on 2026-11-11, after the fixes: a build on a scratch repo with real Codex as the worker and real Claude Code (Haiku) as the admin agent ended `done`: both tasks `verified`, one engine commit per task ('T001: ...', 'T002: ...') plus 'plan: hello', both boxes checked, both files with the right text. The owner's part: one answer to Claude Code's trust question and one to Codex's.

REAL RUN 2, flaw 1: Codex's start showed its update question, then for a moment a bare prompt, then its trust question. The engine took the bare prompt for 'ready', marked the worker `working` and pasted its role line and task line into the trust question. Codex kept the pasted lines and ran them after the trust answer.
REAL RUN 2, flaw 2: while the worker sat at Codex's trust question and no turn had run, the engine ran the task's check, counted one failed attempt, and sent a second prompt version.

REAL RUN 3 on 2026-11-11, after the ready and delivery fixes, on a fresh scratch repo: both trust questions showed under needs-you (kind trust) and nothing was pasted before the answers; after the owner's two answers the build ended `done` in about 45 seconds with no other action; both tasks verified with 0 failed attempts; engine commits 'T001: ...', 'T002: ...', 'plan: hello'; the real admin agent answered an owner's question in the chat during the build.

REAL RUN 4 on 2026-11-11 (Plan stage): after the owner's trust answer, the real admin agent (Claude Code, Haiku) wrote SPEC.md in the chat's feature folder from the SPEC template, and its reply reached the chat. The owner's global fresh-eyes Stop hook fired inside that agent and made it start a reader subagent of its own.

REAL RUN 5 on 2026-11-11 (M1 on a chat with no repo): a reply; Pause during a long turn gave the status `paused`, and Resume gave the finished text; after `tmux kill-session` the next message was answered by a restarted session.

REAL RUN 5, flaw: when the owner's Stop hook made the agent speak again after its answer, the chat showed only the last remark ('The fresh-eyes read is running...') and not the answer ('hello'). The engine writes .md files (agents/admin.prompt.md, inbox files) into the agent's folder, and that is what the owner's hook reacts to.

REAL RUN 5, flaw: after Pause and Resume of the admin agent in the middle of a turn, the owner's message ended as `interrupted` although its answer arrived after Resume, and the chat showed a second copy of the owner's line.

REAL RUN 6 on 2026-11-11, after the two chat fixes: the admin message of a turn with two Stop events held both replies ('hello', then the remark about the owner's fresh-eyes hook); after Pause and Resume in the middle of a turn the owner's message ended `answered` with one owner line. The reply after Resume holds only the text written after 'continue'; the text before the Escape is in the terminal only.
